question: If the volume of the cuboid is 440 cm³ and the area of ​​its base is 88 cm², find the height of the cuboid.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any uniform solid figure like a cylinder or cuboid:

Volume = Base Area × Height

Height = Volume ÷ Base Area

Height = 440 ÷ 88 = 5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of the cuboid = 440 cm³

Area of its base = 88 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cuboid = Base Area × Height

 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
•

 Base Area = 88 cm²
 
 
 
•

 Height = ?
 
 
 Volume = 440 cm³

**Calculations:**

⇒ 440 = 88 × Height

⇒ Height = 440 ÷ 88

⇒ Height = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid

TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl) where l, b, and h are the length, breadth, and height respectively.

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest rod that can fit perfectly inside a cuboid = √(l² + b² + h²).

Lateral Surface Area of a Cuboid

LSA = Area of 4 walls = 2h(l + b). It can also be defined as Perimeter of base × height.
